newsitem.title: USA: Conn. unemployment rate rises to 4.9 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Conn. unemployment rate rises to 4.9 pct in Sept.

text.p: Connecticut on Wednesday said that its unemployment rate in September rose 0.2 percentage points to 4.9 percent, mainly because the manufacturing sector lost 3,800 jobs as defense cutbacks continued.
The state's latest data shows a strong improvement from the year-ago period, when the unemployment rate stood at 5.6 percent.

Nonfarm employment in September rose by 1,300 jobs to 1,584,900, and the government workforce, fattened by the start of the school year, climbed by 4,900 employees. And the service industry stayed strong, gaining 1,800 jobs.

While the transporation and public utility sector added 500 jobs, trade employment dropped by 1,800 due to the end of the summer season. Around 300 mining jobs were lost, though finance, insurance and real estate were flat.
A breakdown of the unemployment in the state's labor markets follows.
These data are not seasonally adjusted.
--Bridgeport, 5.9 percent, up two percentage points from August.
